description: U.S. Bancorp, a financial services holding company, provides various financial services to individuals, businesses, institutional organizations, governmental entities, and other financial institutions
description_full: U.S. Bancorp, a financial services holding company, provides various financial services to individuals, businesses, institutional organizations, governmental entities, and other financial institutions in the United States. The company operates through Wealth, Corporate, Commercial and Institutional Banking; Consumer and Business Banking; Payment Services; and Treasury and Corporate Support segments. It offers depository services, including checking accounts, savings accounts, and time certificate contracts; and lending services, such as traditional credit products and credit card services, lease financing and import/export trade, agricultural finance, asset-backed lending, and other products. The company also provides cash management, capital markets, and trust and investment management services; and ancillary services comprising capital markets, treasury management, and receivable lock-box collection services to corporate and governmental entity customers. In addition, it offers asset management and fiduciary services for individuals, estates, foundations, business corporations, and charitable organizations; and investment and insurance products to its customers principally within its domestic markets, as well as fund administration services to mutual and other funds. Further, the company provides corporate and purchasing card, and corporate trust services; and credit card services, merchant and ATM processing, mortgage banking, insurance, brokerage and leasing services. U.S. Bancorp was founded in 1863 and is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

financial_summary: U.S. Bancorp is a large-cap financial services business with a $87.3B market cap on $28.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +4% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 0.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 15% below the high.

val: The price sits above its blended-model fair value of $42.78 (margin of safety -31%), so there is no valuation cushion.
